answer: Every berth on a jetty ships with a cipher only its holder can solve. A newcomer must present a solved cipher sealed by two unrelated berth holders, and one cipher signs only one newcomer, so relaying it merges the two claims into a single seat. Each additional berth on the same jetty costs its index squared in bond, so n aliases burn about n cubed while still needing n distinct solvers. Standing then climbs a knoll: each tier re-samples a random cipher, and a forged answer voids every claim sharing that seal, so staked silence cannot buy rank.
